expected_effect: Public val_bpb decreases relative to same-host control by 0.002-0.006 (predeclared direction: lower), driven by a step-count increase of +8% to +15% (approx 2240-2390 steps vs 2071-2076) at fixed 1800 s. Minimum to count as SUCCESS: steps >= +2% AND public_val_bpb lower by >= 0.001. If steps rise >= +2% but BPB is not lower than control, the quality-cost hypothesis is falsified (FALSIFIED-QUALITY). If steps change by <= 1%, the throughput hypothesis is falsified (FALSIFIED-INERT). Steps > +10% triggers EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW with matched-step trajectory comparison before any quality claim.
hypothesis: Under the pinned environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1', no compiler matmul autocast) the control executes every consumer of norm() output in FP32: the qkv/out/MLP projections, the embedding-normalization consumers, the local-convolution input, and the final LM-head input (train.py norm() 1446-1462; Block.forward; GPT.forward; Linear.forward selects weight/cache by input dtype). The only isolated precision arm run so far, --bf16-sdpa-input, converted a single boundary to BF16 and recovered +7.6% steps (2233 vs 2076) with better public BPB (1.002028 vs 1.005967). The existing --bf16-norm-output policy converts the much larger share of matmul FLOPs and activation traffic to BF16 (and, as a documented side effect, also delivers BF16 Q/K/V to SDPA because CausalSelfAttention aligns V to Q's dtype and rope_norm preserves input dtype). I hypothesize the complete norm-output precision policy yields a larger fixed-budget step gain (>= +8%) than the SDPA arm and that BF16 rounding of normalized activations at this 55.7M-dense/537M-table scale costs less quality than the extra steps recover, giving lower public BPB than control.
single_causal_change: Pass --bf16-norm-output only. This is the complete existing norm-output precision policy of train.py (not a projection-only cast): all norm() outputs become BF16, so qkv/out/MLP projections, embedding-normalization consumers, local-conv input, the final LM-head input, and (via V-to-Q dtype alignment and dtype-preserving rope_norm) SDPA inputs execute in BF16; FP32 master weights, optimizer state, loss code, evaluator, and every other option stay at 9a4caa7b defaults. No --bf16-sdpa-input, no --ngram-rms-fp32, no --nki-*/--compile-* flag, no optimizer/schedule/batch/architecture/ngram-ve/eval change. Launch shape and environment identical to the pinned controls (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2, torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4, --num-steps 5000, --max-train-seconds 1800, --seed 42, NEURON_CC_FLAGS exactly '--optlevel=1', NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_SEED=42, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1). This arm is NOT an independent boundary from the SDPA KEEP: its scope overlaps and supersedes the SDPA cast; a later stacking run with --bf16-sdpa-input is expected to be near-inert and must be proposed separately with that interaction hypothesis. Pre-full checks from the smoke: resolved precision oneliner shows bf16_norm_output=True and bf16_sdpa_input=False; num_params_M 592.9; ngram_ve oneliner identical to control ('True tables=4 rows=1048576 dim=128 index_gather=True trigram=True opt=rmsprop flat_lr=True bf16=True rms_fp32_state_math=False nki_rms=False'); architecture oneliners identical to control; causality_passed True. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967). ONE authoritative outcome classification, evaluated in order: (1) HALT-SEMANTIC-REVIEW if any pre-full check fails - do not launch the full run; (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if full-run steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control (norm-output precision is not a measurable cost); (4) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if steps > +10% of control (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22): record throughput and BPB; before any quality claim compare the candidate's logged validation trajectory to the control's at matched step counts; if matched-step trajectories are unavailable or noncomparable, quality attribution is recorded unresolved; SUCCESS may be declared only if public_val_bpb < control by >= 0.001 and no matched-step deficit > 0.010 at the control's final step; (5) SUCCESS if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.001; (6) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control (BF16 rounding of normalized activations costs at least as much as the recovered steps); (7) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, including any gain in [0, 0.001) or steps in (+1%, +2%).
